subject: Atlas Bank RFP — Abuse detection telemetry, exportability, and SLA clarifications
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@atlasbank.com>

Cc: procurement@atlasbank.com <procurement@atlasbank.com>

Subject: Atlas Bank RFP — follow-up questions on misuse monitoring

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the RFP package you sent earlier this week. The compliance review team had a few follow-ups specifically around real-time detection, evidence exports, and notification SLAs: 

1) When your detectors flag a conversation for potential policy violation, what telemetry is preserved by default (raw user input, model tokens, system prompts, metadata like session id, IPs)? How long do you retain each type?

2) Can we request automated exports of flagged conversation payloads (redacted as needed) to our S3/secure FTP on an hourly basis? If so, what format and schema do you support?

3) Incident notification SLA: what is your standard SLA for notifying a customer security contact after a high-confidence misuse alert? Are there escalation windows for P1/P2?

4) For auditability, do you provide tamper-evident logs or signed manifests we can ingest into our log-retention system?

We need short, itemized answers and any sample schemas/evidence so we can pass these to our InfoSec and legal teams. Can you also include the most recent SOC 2 auditor contact name and date?

Appreciate a reply by Monday.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Lead Compliance Analyst — Atlas Bank
Samantha.Ortiz@atlasbank.com

Subject: Re: Atlas Bank RFP — follow-up questions on misuse monitoring

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. I grouped responses for quick ingestion by your reviewers and attached a short evidence bundle. Summary answers below; full details and sample exports attached.

1) Telemetry preserved by default:
- User input (raw text): retained for 30 days by default for hosted customers, configurable up to 365 days for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Model I/O tokens (normalized hashes only in hosted; full tokens for Dedicated/Private with customer consent): retained 30 days default.
- System prompts / prompt templates: stored with versioning for 365 days.
- Session metadata (session id, model version, region, request latency): stored 90 days.
- Network identifiers (IP addresses): optional; we recommend customers funnel through their VPC for IP retention.

2) Automated exports to customer S3 / FTP:
- Yes — we support scheduled export of flagged items. Formats: JSONL (recommended), compressed CSV for metadata. Schema: see attached "flagged-conversations-sample.jsonl" and "telemetry-retention-matrix.csv". Exports can be pushed hourly, daily, or on-demand. Encryption in transit (TLS 1.3) + server-side encryption (SSE-S3/SSE-KMS) supported.

3) Incident notification SLA:
- Standard hosted customers: P1 (high-confidence, active exploitation) notification within 1 hour; P2 within 4 hours.
- Dedicated / Enterprise tier (contracted): customizable SLAs down to 15-minute notification windows and on-call paging.
- Notifications: webhook (JSON payload), email, and optional PagerDuty integration. See sample payload in the attachments.

4) Tamper-evident logs / manifests:
- We provide signed manifests (SHA256 + timestamp + signing certificate) for daily export bundles. For Dedicated/Private, customers can opt into HSM-backed signing (bring-your-own-key supported).

SOC 2 auditor: SecureAudit LLP, contact: Priya Menon, last audit report: 2027-03-28 (summary provided in the bundle).

Attachments included: redwood-abuse-observability-bundle.pdf (contains architecture diagrams, exporter configs, sample webhook payloads), flagged-conversations-sample.jsonl, telemetry-retention-matrix.csv

Next steps: happy to run a 30-min technical deep-dive next week to walk your InfoSec through the exporter schema and signing process. I suggested a couple of times below.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Hi Samantha — thanks, and great questions. Short answers and pointers below: 

- Webhook P1 payload schema: each P1 webhook is a single JSON object (no header row) with fields: event_id, detected_at (ISO8601), detection_confidence, policy_id, model_variant, session_id, redaction_level, user_text_hash, user_text_redacted (present only if customer opts into raw export), artifacts_url (signed URL to the daily bundle), and sample_evidence (base64-encoded snippet). Full example in attached redwood-abuse-observability-bundle.pdf and the flagged-conversations-sample.jsonl.

- Hourly S3 export and manifest: yes — every export bundle (hourly/daily) includes a signed manifest (SHA256 + timestamp + signature). We generate the manifest before upload to customer bucket so your WORM system can validate file integrity.

- JSONL format: each line is a standalone event object (no separate header). Metadata about the bundle is included in the signed manifest and in the artifacts_url container metadata.

- SLA measurement point: hosted P1 SLA is measured from detector firing timestamp (we surface both detection_time and enrichment_complete_time in the payload so you can choose how to interpret alerts). For Dedicated/Enterprise contracts we can switch the contractual measurement if desired.

Call: Monday 23rd 10:00am-10:30am PT works for our ops engineer Jonas. I cc'd Jonas to accept and share a calendar invite. We'll also bring a one-page schema PDF on the call.

Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
